title: Diverse mechanisms of therapy resistance in relapsed childhood B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL): a report from the Children’s Oncology Group
description: Relapsed B-ALL generally occurs due to the emergence of subclones resistant to therapy. Using 183 relapsed cases with whole genome and transcriptome sequencing, we showed that relapses can also be caused by a second malignancy or germline predisposition. For the ETV6::RUNX1 subtype, we showed that cases with gain of the fusion allele or with fusion transcript E5-E4 have a higher risk of relapse. For the hyperdiploid subtype, we demonstrated that cases with low modal chromosomal numbers (between 50 and 52) were more prone to relapse than those with >=53 chromosomes, and this factor had an additive effect in association with CREBBP mutations.
